Selected UK Investment Protection Agreements with express territorial extension clauses covering Gibraltar

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Gibraltar: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (as amended), Gibraltar AML/CFT Regulations 2021 (Schedule 1 CDD rules), Sanctions Act 2019 (Gibraltar), Companies Act 2014 (Beneficial Ownership and Overseas Companies provisions), Income Tax (Economic Substance) Act 2019. Bermuda: Companies Act 1981, Proceeds of Crime Act 1997, Anti-Terrorist Financing Act 2002, Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2021 (Bermuda register of beneficial owners), and the Corporate Service Provider Business Act 2000 governing licensed formation agents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Registry General, Ministry of Legal Affairs, Bermuda; recognized in Gibraltar under the Hague Apostille Convention 1961 as extended to both British Overseas Territories

Beneficial Ownership Declaration and UBO structural diagram piercing to ultimate natural persons

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized statutory declaration; consular legalization required only where any ultimate UBO documentation originates from a non-Hague Convention jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity verification evidence (passport, proof of address) for all directors and holders of 25 percent or more of ownership interests

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by Bermuda notary, then Hague Apostille; consular legalization path activated for non-Hague origin documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant or authorized Gibraltar licensed agent, filed with Gibraltar Companies House
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct submission to Gibraltar Registrar; supporting notarized documents follow Hague Apostille chain

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs at or above the 25 percent threshold, directors, senior managers and authorized signatories against: (1) UN Consolidated Sanctions List; (2) UK OFSI Consolidated Sanctions List as extended to Gibraltar under the Sanctions Act 2019; (3) Gibraltar Sanctions List maintained by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission; (4) OFAC SDN List for USD payment rails, Wise and any correspondent banking exposure; (5) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List as a residual benchmark; (6) domestic and international PEP databases including foreign PEPs, family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation is mandatory for any PEP, any person connected with FATF high-risk or grey-listed jurisdictions, or any nominee-flagged structure lacking commercial rationale. CDD must be completed by both the Bermuda licensed CSP and a Gibraltar-appointed AML compliance officer under the AML/CFT Regulations 2021 prior to any registration filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda: Bermuda Department of Registrar of Companies via the Bermuda Government corporate registry portal (https://www.gov.bm/department/registrar-companies). Gibraltar: Gibraltar Companies House online name search and reservation portal (https://www.companieshouse.gi).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Both Bermuda and Gibraltar operate exclusively in English; no transliteration doctrine applies to an English-language exempted company name. The Bermuda Exempted Company name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' as mandated by the Companies Act 1981. In Gibraltar, where the entity registers as an overseas company, the registered name must clearly indicate foreign origin, typically by the marker 'Bermuda' or '(Bermuda)', or otherwise comply with the Companies Act 2014 (Overseas Companies) Regulations to prevent public confusion with a locally incorporated company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicable registrar issues a written notice citing the statutory ground. In Gibraltar, the applicant or its licensed agent may within 21 days of the rejection notice submit a written reconsideration request with legal submissions to the Registrar of Companies; if the refusal is maintained, the decision may be challenged by judicial review in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar within 28 days of the reconsideration decision. In Bermuda, the applicant may request reconsideration under section 15 of the Companies Act 1981 and appeal any final refusal to the Supreme Court of Bermuda by originating summons within 21 days. Recommended strategy: reserve three alternative names concurrently in both registries; and sequence the Gibraltar employment agency licence application ahead of the overseas company registration so that employment-sensitive name tokens are pre-cleared by the competent labour authority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted_Partial. A virtual office arranged through a Bermuda licensed corporate service provider satisfies the Bermudas registered office requirement under section 92 of the Companies Act 1981, and a virtual registered place of business is accepted for the Gibraltar overseas company register. However, an ISIC 7810 Global EOR and contractor payroll agency managed and controlled from Gibraltar must satisfy the Income Tax (Economic Substance) Act 2019 (Gibraltar): payroll processing, employment contract management, bookkeeping, and bank account supervision must be performed in Gibraltar, supported by a physical premises and locally present staff. A pure virtual office without these operational elements will fail the core income-generating activity test and attract corrective penalties of up to GBP 10,000 plus up to 10 percent of turnover where the deficiency persists after an enforcement notice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Assessed at 55 percent probability within the first 12 months of active payroll operations, rising to 70 percent after the first audited return is filed; the Gibraltar Companies Registry, Income Tax Office, and employment agency licensing authority conduct coordinated unannounced inspections of premises, payroll records, employment contracts, and personnel presence, with the EOR sector designated a priority inspection target in the 2024-2025 substance compliance cycle.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981, sections 4(1), 6(1), 7, and 10 (Incorporation of Exempted Companies); Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, Part 23, sections 424-434 (External Companies)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda; Gibraltar Companies House, Registrar of Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Bermuda Exempted Company; Certificate of Incorporation; Form EC-1 Application for Registration of an External Company in Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Bermuda law; the company must issue at least one share in the currency of incorporation. Any premium on shares must be credited to a share premium account. No escrow account is required for incorporation; however, for Gibraltar external registration, the Registrar may require evidence of a local service address and sufficient working capital for the first six months of payroll obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Board approves the allotment and issue of ordinary shares to the subscribers as set out in the Capital Subscription Schedule; each subscriber herewith accepts the corresponding shares at par. (2) The registered office of the Company is fixed at the address specified in the Memorandum of Association and the registered agent shall maintain the same at all times. (3) The following persons are appointed as officers for the ensuing corporate year: [Name] as Director, [Name] as Director, and [Name] as Company Secretary; they are jointly and severally authorised to execute all statutory filings, banking instructions, and service contracts. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and registered agent engagement in Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (online Companies and Partnerships e-Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Bermuda e-Registry and reserve the intended company name by filing a Name Reservation application. Engage a Bermuda-licensed registered agent and provide the agent's Consent to Act letter. After approval, obtain the name reservation confirmation number for use in subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter with licensed Bermuda registered agent
Consent to Act of registered agent
Identity documents and due diligence pack of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, amend the name to include a distinctive element and refile; no additional fee is due upon resubmission within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and filing of incorporation documents in Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscribers execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association and the statutory declaration of compliance (Form 8). The registered agent electronically files the documents, the declaration, and the registration fee schedule through the Bermuda e-Registry. The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation; the same certificate constitutes conclusive evidence of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the declaration, file a corrective statutory declaration and pay any applicable query fee; if rejected for insolvency of subscribers, replace the subscriber and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of shares and first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Bermuda Exempted Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the sole subscriber or director holds the first board meeting and passes the pro forma first board resolution. The minutes record allotment of shares to subscribers, adoption of the registered office, and appointment of directors and company secretary. The resolution is entered in the minute book and the share register is updated.
required_dossiers: Notice and agenda of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director cannot attend in person, use a unanimous written resolution in accordance with the Articles; if any share subscription is void due to withdrawal, reallocate the shares under a supplemental resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gibraltar external company and branch registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House, Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit a certified copy of the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, the constitutional documents, a list of directors, and the Gibraltar service address with Companies House. Complete Form EC-1 (Application for Registration of an External Company) and pay the filing fee. The Registrar will issue a Certificate of Registration for the Gibraltar establishment within five working days.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation
Certified Memorandum and Articles of Association
Corrected list of directors and secretary
Gibraltar registered office and service address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected due to unsworn implicit translations, engage a Gibraltar notary to certify English translations and submit a new Form EC-1 within twenty-one days; for late registration, apply for a penalty reduction in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate tax, social insurance and payroll registration in Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office and Gibraltar Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual corporate tax registration, apply for a tax assessment number, and complete the National Insurance Employer Registration. If confirmed as a Qualifying Company, submit the relevant undertaking form through the Income Tax Office. For EOR operations, also register as a payroll agent with the Social Insurance agency for reporting employers' contributions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration of the Gibraltar branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Social Insurance registration is delayed, submit a payroll undertaking letter and begin filing with a temporary employer number; if the tax office disputes the Qualifying Company status, appeal to the Tax Ombudsman.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, physical and environmental licensing and occupational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Trade, Licensing and Consumer Authority; Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change; Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for an Employment Agency Licence with the GLTCA, including the premises address and responsible manager. Obtain a Fire Safety Certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Authority, and submit an environmental impact registration to the Department of the Environment if applicable. For EOR office operations, a full environmental impact assessment is not required, but an energy and consumption screening is recommended.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership evidence for physical office
Fire safety risk assessment and certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence application is refused, appeal to the Licensing Authority Appeals Panel under section 23 of the Employment Agencies Ordinance; if the environmental classification is upgraded, submit an environmental management plan within thirty days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Trade, Licensing and Consumer Authority (GLTCA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Employment Agency Licence — Global Employer of Record and Staffing Agency Operating Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (Gibraltar)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 'Low-Impact Office and Digital Services' — Registration only; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report is not required for a staff augmentation and payroll service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process machinery; VOC emissions from HVAC in office premises shall meet the thresholds under the Environmental Quality Standards (Air Pollution) Regulations 2019; wastewater containing no industrial effluents may be discharged to the municipal sewer under consent; all confidential records must be shredded and disposed of under the Waste Management Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service; structural load capacity certificate for any premises above 500 sq ft; occupational health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar) covering workplace ergonomics, electrical safety, and emergency exit access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar - Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax); portal: https://www.gibratax.gi. Corporate registration: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies House; customs: HM Customs Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Bermuda Exempted Company as an external company under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 within one month of establishing a place of business (file certified Bermuda certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director/secretary particulars, Gibraltar registered-office address, appoint Gibraltar resident agent/manager). Step 2: Apply for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) with the Income Tax Office (Gibratax) using the approved company registration form; attach the Companies House registration certificate and constitutional documents; engage a Gibraltar tax agent. Step 3: Register as an employer under the Gibraltar PAYE and Social Insurance schemes if hiring Gibraltar-based staff (mandatory for EOR substance). Step 4: If physical goods are imported, obtain an importer/declarant code from HM Customs Gibraltar. Step 5: File annual Gibraltar corporate tax returns even if no chargeable income arises. Precondition: obtain an employment agency licence under the Gibraltar Employment Act for EOR/staffing activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope - the Bermuda Exempted Company is tax-exempt in Bermuda by exempted-company election, but its Gibraltar branch/activity is taxed by Gibraltar only on chargeable income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar (Income Tax Act 2010). EOR and payroll service fees generated through Gibraltar-based activity are chargeable at 12.5% corporation tax; foreign-source income not arising or received in Gibraltar is outside the Gibraltar charge.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Gibraltar. Available mechanisms: (i) Qualifying Company / finance-centre income exemption application under the Income Tax Act 2010 for specified qualifying categories, subject to economic substance conditions; (ii) Gibraltar group relief elections; (iii) capital allowance pooling and transfer elections; (iv) hybrid mismatch alignment/reporting elections under OECD/EU ATAD-aligned hybrid mismatch rules (effective 1 January 2020); (v) Bermuda exempted-status election with the Bermuda Registrar (no impact on Gibraltar tax).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax in Gibraltar; the territory is outside the EU VAT area and outside UK VAT (Value Added Tax Act 1994, Schedule 1). Gibraltar imposes only narrow customs and excise duties on specified physical goods under the Customs Ordinance 2012 (alcohol, tobacco, fuel, certain imports). Cross-border EOR and contractor payroll services are outside the scope of any Gibraltar indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no VAT/GST registration threshold exists because no VAT/GST system is in force. No indirect tax registration is required for pure service/EOR activities. Importers of physical goods must obtain an importer code from HM Customs Gibraltar (no de minimis threshold; duty arises on first importation; reliefs exist for temporary admission and re-export).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Gibraltar imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, SII/SAF-T/CFDI-style e-invoicing, or mandatory fiscal-authority API connection. Invoicing follows general commercial law; accounting records and invoice evidence must be retained for at least 6 years under the Income Tax Act 2010. Customs declarations (electronic or manual) apply only to physical-goods movements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable - Gibraltar has no VAT to zero-rate. Cross-border EOR/payroll services rendered to non-Gibraltar clients are not subject to any Gibraltar indirect tax and require no 0% VAT claim or refund mechanism. For physical goods, customs-duty relief may be achieved by export-processing, temporary-admission, or duty-drawback regimes under the Customs Ordinance 2012; no VAT refund exists.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Execution-only evidence for EOR payroll services: invoices, master EOR agreement, and underlying client/contractor employment contracts
Gibraltar PAYE and social insurance records, payroll runs evidencing local substance
Inward remittance records (SWIFT MT103 / Wise payment confirmations) evidencing foreign client receipts
Where physical goods are in scope: Gibraltar Customs export declaration (SAD-equivalent) and bill of lading / air waybill
Statement of nil-Gibraltar-source income with jurisdictional sourcing analysis if foreign-source income treatment is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or fraudulent declarations attract penalties under the Income Tax Act 2010: misdeclaration penalties up to 100% of tax undercharged plus interest at statutory rates, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent evasion including fines and imprisonment. Abusive customs-duty relief claims are clawed back under the Customs Ordinance 2012 with penalties up to three times the duty evaded and forfeiture of goods. For EOR service income mischaracterised as foreign-source to escape Gibraltar charge, the Commissioner may re-source the income, apply the GAAR and transfer-pricing rules, and issue retrospective assessments with interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: There is no independent central bank of Gibraltar. The Bank of England anchors monetary policy for the Sterling area, the Government of Gibraltar issues the Gibraltar Pound (GIP) at a fixed 1:1 parity with GBP, and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the competent supervisor for banks, payment institutions, and electronic-money institutions. The operative exchange-control framework is the residual and suspended UK Exchange Control Act 1947 (as extended to Gibraltar), under which no exchange-control permits, consents, or licensing are required for bona fide current or capital transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility for GIP against GBP, EUR, and USD. There are no current-account or capital-account exchange restrictions applicable to a Bermuda Exempted Company operating a global EOR payroll platform with treasury functions routed through Gibraltar. Client fee receipts, payroll funding remittances, intercompany shareholder loans, and profit remittances may flow freely in any convertible currency without exchange-control approval. The only practical hurdles are GFSC/AML source-of-funds verification, CRS/FATCA filing classification, and standard banking confirmation of the commercial purpose of each flow. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to beneficial-ownership identification and tax-transparency reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. The United Kingdom abolished mandatory surrender of export proceeds in 1979, and Gibraltar applies the same deregulated framework. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation, no minimum conversion ratio, and no designation into state-controlled clearing accounts for export-of-services receipts such as EOR client fees and payroll margins. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in any freely convertible currency; only standard GFSC record-keeping, accounting, and AML/CFT transaction-monitoring obligations apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: MEDIUM-HIGH viability with mandatory structural safeguards. Gibraltar has no unlicensed EMI sector: electronic-money institutions require GFSC authorisation under the Financial Services (Electronic Money) Regulations 2011 and the Payment Services Act, and may passport into the UK under the preserved UK-Gibraltar financial-services arrangement. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Revolut Business) can onboard this Bermuda Exempted Co for bulk contractor payroll disbursement and virtual-IBAN segregation, but they cannot take deposits or hold the treasury's capital escrow beyond safeguarding thresholds. The blueprint therefore mandates a tier-1 Gibraltar authorised bank as master-account custodian, with the EMI deployed solely as a disintermediating, low-value payroll clearing rail. GFSC-regulated EMIs will also apply enhanced sector-level due-diligence to staffing and EOR platforms.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory mandate for physical appearance exists under Gibraltar AML/CFT law: CDD may be satisfied through certified copies, electronic verification, and reliance on a Gibraltar-licensed professional introducer under the GFSC AML/CFT Handbook. In practice, NatWest International and Jyske typically require at least one director or the appointed corporate-services officer to attend an in-person interview at a Gibraltar branch or an approved UK/offshore centre, unless a GFSC-regulated firm provides a formal introducer attestation. Remote account opening for the Bermuda Exempted Co is legally available where a Gibraltar-licensed corporate-services provider acts as registered-office and substance agent, a notarised board resolution and certified UBO register are couriered, a video interview is conducted, and signatory biometric verification is completed. Realistic onboarding period is 2-4 weeks, reducing to 1-2 weeks when a trusted introducer is engaged.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity of the Bermuda Exempted Company (historical bearer-share model and nominee director structures).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated Bermuda Registrar search report; Certificate of Good Standing; certified Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws; Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register extract; ultimate-UBO chain chart with passport and proof-of-address for each natural person; current registered-agent and principal-office confirmation from the Bermuda corporate-services provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-privileged structure flag: 0% Bermuda tax combined with Gibraltar offshore status may be interpreted as tax-evasion or source-of-funds risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda and Gibraltar counsel tax opinions confirming OECD/CRS/FATCA compliance; group FATCA GIIN and CRS registration records; intercompany transfer-pricing documentation for EOR margins; written commercial rationale for the Bermuda holding / Gibraltar treasury / EOR destination operating-entity split; group audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border payroll to 100+ contractors in multiple jurisdictions triggers transaction-monitoring alerts and potential sanctions-corridor screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete contractual stack for the EOR portfolio (client agreements, contractor staffing contracts, works orders, payroll runbooks, payslips); evidence of statutory payroll and social-security filings per destination country; pre-release sanctions and PEP screening records for all beneficiaries; transaction-narrative methodology; independent AML expert opinion confirming the Low_Risk_Standard classification under UK and Gibraltarian risk factors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed-activity concern: Gibraltar employment-agency licensing or Gibraltar payment-services licensing of the Bermuda Co's treasury and payroll functions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar Employment Agency/Bureau licence where physical placement activity occurs in Gibraltar, or a legal opinion confirming exemption for remote EOR services rendered to non-Gibraltar clients; payment-services opinion confirming the company pays only its own payroll obligations and performs no third-party payment service; GFSC-regulated EMI support letter documenting the sponsored payment-correspondence relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance deficit: management and control purportedly exercised from Gibraltar without physical offices, employees, or locally documented decisions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance dossier comprising Gibraltar office lease and utility invoices; employment contracts for Gibraltar-based finance/compliance personnel; minutes of board meetings physically held in Gibraltar; registered-office certificate; substance opinion mapping each income stream to real economic activities across Bermuda, Gibraltar, and the EOR destination jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inward remittance stack: (i) settle via SWIFT MT103 (GBP via CHAPS/Faster Payments; EUR via TARGET2/SEPA correspondent; USD via Fedwire/CHIPS) from the parent or shareholder to the Gibraltar master account; (ii) include an unambiguous purpose narrative such as 'Equity capital contribution / share premium' or 'Shareholder loan — intercompany funding' with a balance-of-payments code aligned to direct investment or other capital transfers, never 'service fees' on an equity leg; (iii) pre-clear each injection with the receiving bank by submitting a certified board resolution approving the capital contribution, a source-of-wealth statement of the remitting party, and audited accounts of the remitter; (iv) credit the funds to a separately styled 'Capital Escrow / Share Premium' sub-account before transferring to the operational payroll account; (v) maintain an injection register for CRS/FATCA, economic substance, and audit evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payroll and contractor clearing rail map: (i) UK/Northern Ireland salaries through Faster Payments for normal run-rate and CHAPS for high-value or final settlements, with HMRC RTI reporting attached; (ii) Eurozone contractors through SEPA Credit Transfer, including SEPA Instant for same-day disbursements, from the bank's EUR account or an authorised EMI's segregated framework; (iii) rest-of-world contractors through SWIFT MT103 with strict salary or contractor-fee narratives and full beneficiary identification; (iv) bulk multi-country payroll through Wise Business/Airwallex virtual-IBAN sub-routes under the GFSC-authorised master bank, safeguarded and reconciled daily; (v) commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) are non-standard for ISIC 7810 EOR services and are preserved only for any ancillary goods-trade treasury line; (vi) STP governance requires digitised payroll files, beneficiary static-data validation, pre-release sanctions screening, and FX conversion executed no earlier than T-2 to lock rates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts (OTC) on GBP/EUR and GBP/USD for fixed-rate payroll funding up to six months, executed under an ISDA 2002 or FSFMA master confirmation with the tier-1 Gibraltar bank
FX swap transactions (buy/sell spot versus forward) for treasury liquidity alignment between GIP/GBP, EUR, and USD accounts
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CIRS/CCS) for matching long-dated EUR or USD payroll funding liabilities against GBP capital positions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for hedging contractor payroll obligations in restricted or emerging-market currencies (INR, IDR, NGN, EGP, BRL) where deliverable forwards are unavailable
Purchased European-style FX options (OTC), plain vanilla calls/puts on EUR/USD/GBP, utilised only as hedges and never sold uncovered, to cap maximum payroll cost

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation; alternatively by 31 July for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs BMD 50 per day capped at BMD 500; persistent non-filing triggers administrative strike-off and forfeiture of assets to the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days after the anniversary of the Gibraltar branch registration or the end of the accounting reference period, whichever is later
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalty of £150, escalating to £5,000; directors can be criminally liable; repeated default results in removal (strike-off) of the branch registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Beneficial Ownership Secure Search database)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within 14 days after the annual return filing; any share transfer must be updated in the BOSS register within 21 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to £500 for each failure; continued non-compliance is an offence with fines up to £10,000 and imprisonment for directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for the Bermuda exempted company if gross assets exceed BMD 5 million, share capital subscriptions exceed BMD 1 million, assets under management exceed BMD 2 million, or the company holds a regulated Gibraltar EOR/staffing licence requiring audited accounts. The EOR staffing agency requires a certified independent audit in Gibraltar annually, regardless of turnover, because the staffing licence is regulated under the Employment Agency Ordinance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; the Gibraltar branch may prepare financial statements under FRS 102 for local filing; the Bermuda holding entity may adopt IFRS for consolidated statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Gibraltar register is not publicly accessible; the registered agent must file the annual confirmation of beneficial owners with the BOSS database at the time of the annual return. Any transfer of shares in the Bermuda exempted company must be notified to the Gibraltar agent within 21 days and the BOSS record updated; the Bermuda exempted company must also maintain its own beneficial ownership register at the registered office and confirm it annually to the Bermuda registered agent.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,800 to US$3,500 per year for a Gibraltar corporate-services provider and registered office; Bermuda registered agent and registered office US$1,200 to US$2,800
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$12,000 to US$22,000 for a licensed EOR entity with payroll platform; US$6,000 to US$10,000 for the Bermuda exempted parent if audited

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 10% flat corporate income tax rate on assessable profits (Income Tax Act 2010, as amended); no progressive corporate bands and no surtax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential rate regimes; legacy exempt-company annual-fee positions are in run-off and confer no rate reduction. Effective base is reduced by statutory capital allowances, employer pension and payroll costs, and the territorial rule under which foreign-source EOR platform fees are assessed only if accrued in or remitted to Gibraltar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1 (Company Tax Return); filed with the Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar via the Income Tax Office electronic filing portal or by paper submission to the Income Tax Office, Gibraltar.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (by accounting period; accounts spanning a 30 June year-of-assessment end may trigger two return periods).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within nine months after the end of the year of assessment (1 July to 30 June), i.e. no later than 31 March immediately following the 30 June tax-year end; the Comptroller of Income Tax may issue an estimated assessment where a return is not received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: registered company name, Gibraltar company number, registered office, and status of accounting officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm a physical registered office in Gibraltar; ensure the file shows the non-resident directors' appointments and any local agent of record.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period: start and end dates of the accounts year, prepared in GIP or GBP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the period exactly with the EOR payroll cut-off; reconcile Wise and Local Payroll Direct Debit statements to the period boundary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income: total EOR service fees (management fee and client recharges) after excluding pass-through payroll disbursements made by the EOR as agent for the client employer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain contractual schedules distinguishing the pure pass-through salary flow from the service margin; only the net margin and recharges are assessable on the Gibraltarian EOR entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: employee wages, statutory social insurance, platform and software costs, professional fees, rent, and utilities attributable to the EOR trade.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow non-arm's-length intercompany recharges; attach transfer pricing schedules for any payments to overseas staffing affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted trading profit/(loss): net profit after Box 4, capital allowances, and any recognized loss carry-forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit audited financial statements with the return; the Comptroller may reject the loss claim if no continuity of trade or substance evidence is provided.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax charge at 10% and double taxation relief: computation of tax on Box 5 and credit for qualifying foreign withholding taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a Certificate of Tax Residence and treaty claim forms where UK source royalties or interest relief is sought; state the remittance-basis position where foreign-source fees are not remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or repayment claimed: balance due after installments, with the GIP bank reference of the electronic transfer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay from the Gibraltar bank account; overseas wire payments should cite the Form 1 assessment ID to avoid misallocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Automatic late-filing penalty of GIP 100, rising by GIP 50 per month up to GIP 1,000; tax-geared penalties up to 100% of the under-assessed tax plus a 50% uplift for deliberate concealment; interest at 8% per annum on unpaid tax; criminal prosecution for willful failure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Gibraltar imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by a Gibraltar company to any shareholder, resident or non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Gibraltar's only comprehensive DTA is the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Agreement (in force from 16 July 2020). To claim relief on UK-source payments: (1) apply to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for a Gibraltar Certificate of Tax Residence confirming treaty residence and the EOR activity; (2) complete the relevant HMRC treaty claim form and attach the TRC; (3) provide the TRC and claim form to the UK payer to apply the 0% rate; (4) for outbound payments from Gibraltar no relief procedure is required because Gibraltar levies no withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 0% withholding on both royalties and interest paid by a Gibraltar company. Treaty: UK-Gibraltar DTA reduces UK-source interest to 0% and royalties to 0% for a Gibraltar-resident beneficial owner; the limited-beneficiary clause must be satisfied for platform/IP royalties received by the EOR entity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Gibraltar monetary threshold is published; the Income Tax Office applies an OECD-aligned materiality test. Practical safe harbor: prepare a Local File when controlled cross-border EOR transactions exceed GIP 1,000,000 per year and a Master File when group consolidated revenue exceeds GIP 50,000,000; maintain a benchmarking study where an intercompany service margin falls outside the interquartile range (typically 3%-7% for low-risk EOR administration).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Income Tax (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019 apply to a Gibraltar-resident company carrying on a Relevant Activity; a global EOR and contractor payroll platform falls within the headquarters/service-centre category. The company must in Gibraltar: (i) hold and document board meetings directing the EOR trade; (ii) employ staff adequate in number and seniority relative to the payroll headcount administered; (iii) maintain a physical office; (iv) incur expenditure proportionate to gross revenue; and (v) perform core income-generating activities (client contracting, payroll computation and disbursement, statutory reporting to each host jurisdiction) locally. Delegation to non-Gibraltar affiliates is permitted only if supervised from Gibraltar; failure triggers financial penalties, exchange of information with HMRC, and adjustment of the territorial basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of EOR contract service fees from gross income, false invoicing to offshore staffing clients, or re-characterizing service margins as pass-through 'loans' without any arm's-length agreement or substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Interest at 8% per annum on unpaid tax, tax-geared penalties of up to 100% of the under-assessed tax plus a 50% concealment uplift; on conviction a court fine at discretion and/or imprisonment up to 7 years under the Income Tax Act 2010 and Criminal Justice Act 2011.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors may be personally assessed for the tax where assets were dissipated, disqualified for up to 15 years, and subject to travel restraints during mutual legal assistance and confiscation proceedings; fraudulent trading triggers unlimited personal contribution under the Companies Act 2014.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a mailbox Gibraltar entity with nominee directors booking EOR revenue while all payroll, contracting, and client-facing work is performed abroad with no premises, staff, or board activity in Gibraltar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of up to GIP 10,000 per substance category plus continuing daily default penalties; the Income Tax Office will cancel territorial-remittance treatment, re-open assessments, and exchange the file with HMRC under the UK-Gibraltar exchange of information provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil restitution for the tax shortfall, formal disqualification from office, and exposure to Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 confiscation orders; courts may impose travel bans pending determination.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing client payroll funds without customer due diligence, AML compliance officer appointment, or suspicious activity reporting; disbursing salaries to fictitious employees or routing funds to sanctioned jurisdictions through Wise or direct-debit rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and Gibraltar AML Regulations, up to GIP 250,000 fine and/or 14 years' imprisonment for money laundering; the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission may suspend payment operations and impose daily compounding penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability for consenting directors; trading disqualification; confiscation and freezing orders over personal assets; travel bans and surrender of passports are available where flight risk is shown.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated cross-border intercompany transactions (marketing fees to group affiliates, rebilled contractor costs) exceeding the documentation threshold without Local File, benchmarking, or arm's-length margin evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of profits to the arm's-length result, 100% tax-geared penalties on the uplifted amount, daily late-documentation surcharges, and exposure to aligned UK HMRC inquiries through the exchange mechanism.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed inaccurate TP declarations may be personally liable for the penalty uplift, disqualified as directors, and named in mutual tax assistance requests limiting international travel and banking.
